The 6fa3a10 artwork is good - smooth disc, crisp serif "LP", clean waves - but its bilingual wordmark rendered at ~35% opacity and read as grey mush on the dark marquee. Fixed by scaling alpha x2.1 (tasks/repair-built-marks.py LIFT_ALPHA), which lifts the wordmark to solid white and leaves the disc and the knocked-out "LP" counter untouched. CAUTION: an earlier pass read this as an inverted mark and reverted to 6510ac5, which is a much cruder trace with a broken "LP" and an illegible wordmark. It scored better on the blur gate only because hard-edged traces have narrower antialiasing bands than smooth artwork - do not trust that metric alone on this mark. Still profile-derived; official artwork would improve it further.

The "C" monogram shipped as a translucent plate (mean alpha 132/255) beside a solid-white wordmark, so the mark read two-tone on the dark marquee. Solidified; see build-client-logo-pack.solidify_alpha.

The aperture symbol shipped as a flat translucent plate (mean alpha 110/255, sd 13.9) beside a solid-white wordmark. Solidified; blur 1.84 -> 0.45. Still a 150 DPI page crop - needs the client's brand kit for a sharp mark.

Seal shipped with 64% of its ink at partial alpha, rendering as a grey ghost; solidified (blur 1.74 -> 0.44), but the rim text is still unreadable at served size. Official artwork not reachable from this environment - the egress policy denies every brand host. Needs the client's brand kit or a fetch from an allowed network.

Ships reading "TOP GRILI": build-client-logo-pack applies trim_right=0.86 to the source, which slices the wordmark mid-glyph, and a grey remnant of the background box survives regardless. The discarded pixels are not recoverable from the built PNG - re-crop assets/profile-client-logos/top-grill.png, or supply brand artwork.
